approach: With no applied force besides gravity and a frictionless incline, both blocks would accelerate at the same rate on their own, so they need no push from each other.

steps.text: On a smooth incline with no applied force, a block's acceleration along the slope depends only on gravity and the incline angle, not on its mass.
steps.equation: a = g sin30°, the same value for both blocks

steps.text: Since both blocks would accelerate at the same rate even if they were separate, no contact force is needed for them to move together.
The normal contact force between the two blocks is therefore zero.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the heavier 4 kg block pushes on the lighter 2 kg block because it sits lower on the slope, missing that acceleration on a smooth incline does not depend on mass.
Computing a contact force from the mass difference, such as (4−2)g sin30° = 10 N; no such formula exists — a contact force appears only when the two blocks would accelerate at different rates.
